sections.normalized_html: Equilateral triangle [MATH: S] has a side length of [MATH: x] centimeters. Equilateral triangle [MATH: T] has a perimeter that is [MATH: 15] centimeters less than the perimeter of triangle [MATH: S.] What is the function [MATH: A] that represents the area of triangle [MATH: T,] in square centimeters, where [MATH: x > 5?]
sections.readable_text: Equilateral triangle [MATH: S] has a side length of [MATH: x] centimeters. Equilateral triangle [MATH: T] has a perimeter that is [MATH: 15] centimeters less than the perimeter of triangle [MATH: S.] What is the function [MATH: A] that represents the area of triangle [MATH: T,] in square centimeters, where [MATH: x > 5?]

sections.normalized_html:
Let

  • [MATH: x] be the side length of equilateral triangle [MATH: S,] and

  • [MATH: y] be the side length of equilateral triangle [MATH: T.]

Then,

  • the perimeter of triangle [MATH: S] is [MATH: 3x,] and

  • the perimeter of triangle [MATH: T] is [MATH: 3y.]

We are told that the perimeter of triangle [MATH: T] is [MATH: 15] centimeters less than the perimeter of triangle [MATH: S.] In symbols, this means that [MATH: 3y = 3x - 15.]

Since we want to find an expression for the area of triangle [MATH: T,] we solve this equation for [MATH: y{:}] [MATH: 3y|= 3x − 15; (3y)/(3)|= (3x − 15)/(3); y|= x − 5]

Therefore, the function [MATH: A] that represents the area of triangle [MATH: T] is given by [MATH: A(x)|= (sqrt(3))/(4)y^{2}; = (sqrt(3))/(4)(x − 5)^{2}.]
